newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Danka buys Kodak Office Imaging.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Danka buys Kodak Office Imaging.

text.p: Britain's Danka Business Systems Plc on Monday said it agreed to buy Eastman Kodak's Office Imaging and facilities management businesses for $684 million in cash in a move which it said will put it in a leading position in the fastest-growing segment of its market.
Danka's shares soared 82.5 pence to 557.5 pence on the London Stock Exchange following the announcement.
"This puts us in a leading position in the fastest-growing segment of our market, the high-volume market," Danka chairman Mark Vaughan-Lee told Reuters in an interview.

The high-volume market -- photocopiers capable of handling a high humber of pages per minute -- is the fastest-growing segment of the photocopier business and accounts for 43 percent of the North American market. Kodak is one of only three manufacturers of high-volume photocopiers and the only one to allow distribution by third parties.
Danka got its entree into the high-volume market in September 1995 when it agreed to distribute Kodak products in North America. The agreement laid the ground work for the acquisition.

"We got to know their people, their very fine service," Vaughan-Lee said. "When Kodak in January of '96 announced it was seeking to reposition their Office Imaging business, we registered our interest.
"We were not alone in showing an interest," he added.

Kodak originally was marketing the manufacturing side of its business as well as the marketing, sales and service side. Danka, however, is not a manufacturer and was not interested in acquiring that side of the business, Vaughan-Lee said.
In addition to strengthening its position in high-volume copiers, Vaughan-Lee said the acquisition will allow Danka to offer its customers a full range of products and service.
"We'll be able to jointly go to customers and offer the full range of machines, the full range of service," he said. "Customers want to deal with oonly one point of contact."

Danka will also set up a strategic alliance with Kodak, under which Kodak will supply high volume copiers and printers to Danka, which will become the principal distributor of Kodak-branded office copiers and printers.

Danka said it would take a one-off restructuring charge of $25-35 million on the deal in its third-quarter results for integration of the Kodak acquisitions but the purchase should be earnings-enhancing in the first 12 months of operations.
The acquisition will be funded with bank debt under a six-year, $1.2 billion fully underwritten commitment, which will also refinace Danka's existing debt and revolving credit facilties.
It said the business resulting from the acquisition would offer global coverage in office products and services with over 700 offices in 35 countries worldwide.
The deal would bring Danka's yearly sales to around $3.5 billion and its recurring revenue stream from service, supplies and rentals would double to over $2 billion.
